subject: Re: Request for SLA credit after 2026-02-08 impact
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bluecrest.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-08T09:03:12Z
Subject: Outage on 2026-02-08 - request for SLA credit

Hi Monica,

We recorded a disruption to model inference for our production endpoints between 02:22 UTC and 05:27 UTC on 2026-02-08 that impacted customer-facing job processing. Our ops team captured the attached timeline (bluecrest_incident_timeline.pdf) and has logged the impact as ~185 minutes of total downtime across two regions.

Per section 4.2 of our SLA (99.9% monthly uptime), we'd like to kick off a formal request for an SLA service credit for the affected billing period (Feb 1–28). Can you confirm eligibility and the calculation you'll use to determine the credit amount?

For reference: our committed monthly spend under DEAL-7842 is $28,500. We can provide any additional telemetry if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Site Reliability Manager
BlueCrest Logistics

Attachments: bluecrest_incident_timeline.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-08T11:20:05Z
Subject: Re: Outage on 2026-02-08 - request for SLA credit

Hi Samir — thanks for the timeline and for flagging the minutes. Really sorry for the disruption. I’ve received the timeline and will coordinate with billing and legal to validate the eligibility and calculation.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll run the uptime calculation against the Feb billing window and confirm the exact seconds/minutes we count as downtime.
- Loop in finance (Rafael) for the credit amount and accounting treatment.
- Legal will confirm any contractual wording.

I’m cc’ing Marissa (CS) so she can coordinate any product-level remediation notes you want surfaced to customer success and product. I’ll get back to you with a proposal by EOD Tuesday (2026-02-09).

Apologies again — we appreciate your patience.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-09T08:15:00Z
Subject: Fwd: BlueCrest - SLA credit request (DEAL-7842) — please advise

Forwarding BlueCrest request. Key facts at top:
- Impact window per customer: 2026-02-08 02:22–05:27 UTC (~185 minutes reported).
- Billing period: 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28 (28 days = 40320 minutes).
- Committed monthly amount for the deal: $28,500.

Proposed approach (please confirm or correct):
1) Calculate monthly uptime percentage = (total minutes in billing period - downtime minutes) / total minutes in billing period.
   - Example: (40320 - 185) / 40320 = 0.99541 => 99.541% uptime.
2) SLA threshold = 99.9% for this contract (per SLA Appendix). If monthly uptime < 99.9%, eligible for service credits per section 4.3.
3) Service credit calculation per contract: pro rata credit up to 10% of monthly recurring charges for 100% breach banding. Contract language: "For each 0.1% below 99.9%, customer receives 1% of monthly charges, capped at 10%."
   - Using the example above: 99.9 - 99.541 = 0.359% below threshold => credit = 3.59% of monthly charges (rounded per accounting).
   - Credit amount (estimate): 0.0359 * $28,500 = $1,023.15 (we typically round to nearest dollar).

I attached an initial calc (uptime_calc.xlsx) that shows these steps. Requesting: Rafael — can you confirm the accounting treatment and final credit amount that can be issued? Laura — please confirm the legal language we should include (does issuing the credit satisfy contract obligations, any non-waiver language needed). Markus/Marissa — any technical or CS notes we should attach to the customer comms.

Attachments: uptime_calc.xlsx

Thanks — aiming to finalize by mid-day 2026-02-09 so we can communicate to the customer on 2026-02-10.

—Monica

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-09T10:42:37Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueCrest - SLA credit request (DEAL-7842) — please advise

Monica — I reviewed the uptime_calc.xlsx and agree with the methodology. A few notes:
- Using 28-day month (customer provided) yields total minutes 40320. Downtime confirmed as 185 minutes per customer's timeline.
- Percentage below 99.9% = 0.359% => credit = 3.59% of $28,500 = $1,023.15. We will round to $1,023.
- Accounting impact: apply as an invoice credit on the next billing cycle; if there is no upcoming invoice we can apply an account credit and reflect it on the following invoice.
- Please prepare an invoice credit memo referencing INV-8932 (BlueCrest latest invoice). We’ll route the credit memo through finance and attach credit_approval_signed.pdf once countersigned by Legal.

I approve issuance of $1,023 as service credit.

—Rafael Mendes
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit_approval_signed.pdf (placeholder for final signature)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-09T14:01:50Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueCrest - SLA credit request (DEAL-7842) — legal review

Monica / Rafael — legal has reviewed the proposed credit language and amount. Approved with these two clarifications to include in external comms:
1) State the credit is issued "without admission of liability".
2) Include a short non-waiver sentence: "Issuance of this credit does not constitute a waiver of any future claims or rights by either party under the Agreement."

Once finance prepares the credit memo (Rafael), legal will countersign the approval PDF. No further edits required.

—Laura Bennett
General Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-02-10T09:30:00Z
Subject: SLA credit issued for Feb billing window — BlueCrest (DEAL-7842)

Hi Samir — following up with the outcome of your SLA credit request. Thank you for the detailed timeline and patience while we reviewed.

Summary of resolution:
- Impact window accepted: 2026-02-08 02:22–05:27 UTC.
- Downtime minutes counted: 185 minutes during Feb billing window (Feb 1–28).
- Monthly uptime = (40320 - 185) / 40320 = 99.541% (below 99.9% SLA threshold).
- Credit calculation per contract: 3.59% of monthly charges => calculated credit = $1,023 (rounded).

Action taken:
- Finance has approved and will issue a credit memo referencing INV-8932. The credit of $1,023 will be applied to BlueCrest’s next invoice. If you prefer the credit appear as an account balance instead, let me know and we’ll adjust.
- Legal note (per cc): Credit is issued without admission of liability and does not waive any party rights under the Agreement.
- Attached: incident_postmortem.pdf (finalized postmortem) and the calculation spreadsheet (uptime_calc.xlsx).

We regret the disruption. Marissa from CS will follow up separately to review any product-level mitigations and ensure your team has the telemetry needed to confirm continuity.

If you’d like a short call to walk through the postmortem, I’m available tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_postmortem.pdf, uptime_calc.xlsx
